title: Chartwise etale permanence for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Call a morphism $f:X\to Y$ chartwise etale if for every representable etale map $U\to X$ from a scheme $U$, the composite $U\to Y$ is representable etale; representable etale means that every base change to a scheme is an etale morphism of schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a morphism whose source is a scheme, chartwise etale is equivalent to representable etale. Identity morphisms are chartwise etale. Composites of chartwise etale morphisms are chartwise etale, and their base changes by arbitrary morphisms of algebraic spaces are chartwise etale. If $X\to Z$ and $Y\to Z$ are chartwise etale, every morphism $X\to Y$ over $Z$ is chartwise etale. A family is an etale covering when all its maps are chartwise etale and it is jointly surjective on field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. Isomorphisms give singleton etale coverings; composites of etale coverings are etale coverings; and for every etale covering $\{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ and every map $X'\to X$, the family $\{X'\times_XX_i\to X'\}_{i\in I}$ is an etale covering. The fibre products here are sheaf fibre products of algebraic spaces [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 03FR (definition-etale), paragraph following it and Tags 03FT (lemma-composition-etale), 03FU (lemma-base-change-etale), 03FV (lemma-etale-permanence); etale covering axioms: literature/stacks-project/spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F (lemma-etale), clauses (1)-(3).

proof.text: Every map $U\to F$ from a scheme to an algebraic space is representable. Indeed, for a scheme $T\to F$, the sheaf $U\times_F T$ is the pullback of the representable diagonal $F\to F\times F$ along the scheme $U\times_S T\to F\times F$. It is therefore a scheme by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [def-pc-fibre-product]. The identification follows on each test scheme: both sides consist of a pair of maps to $U,T$ with equal images in $F$. In all later steps, this also proves that a fibre product of two schemes over an algebraic space is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 025W (lemma-representable-diagonal), the formal diagonal test; algebraic-space definition Tag 025Y

proof.text: We first record the scheme-test calculations for representable maps; these do not assume chartwise permanence. For representable etale maps $A\to B\to C$ and a scheme $T\to C$, the pullback of their composite factors as the two etale scheme maps $T\times_C A\to T\times_C B\to T$. It is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2). For a base change along $C'\to C$, its pullback to a scheme $T\to C'$ is just $T\times_C A\to T$, so representable etaleness is preserved by definition [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Isomorphisms are representable etale: their scheme tests are isomorphisms, hence open immersions by [def-weil-open-immersion], hence etale by clause (1) of the same scheme lemma. For representable surjective etale maps these arguments also preserve surjectivity: in the composite both scheme projections are surjective and [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition] applies; for a base change the scheme test is the original test. When a surjective etale scheme map is pulled back along another scheme map, the two properties follow from [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. In particular an etale scheme morphism is representable etale, since all its scheme tests are etale by the same base-change lemma. All fibre-product identifications here send a compatible tuple of sections to the same tuple and are inverse by their projections.

source.place: Representable-property scheme tests used in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03EC(1); scheme Tags 02GN, 02GP, 02GO, 01RZ, 01S1

proof.text: If $f:U\to Y$ has scheme source and is chartwise etale, test it on $\operatorname{id}_U$, which is representable etale by step 2. This says exactly that $f$ is representable etale. Conversely, if $f$ is representable etale, its composite with every representable etale scheme chart of $U$ is representable etale by step 2; thus it is chartwise etale. This uses the scheme-test meaning of representability and etaleness in [def-trf-algebraic-space], rather than asserting that all chartwise etale maps with arbitrary source are representable.

source.place: Tag 03FR, paragraph immediately following the definition; scheme-source specialization

proof.text: Here is the source descent calculation needed below. Let $q:U\to F$ have scheme source, and let $p:V\to U$ be a surjective etale scheme map such that $qp$ is representable etale. For any scheme $T\to F$, step 1 makes $U_T=U\times_F T$ and $V_T=V\times_F T$ schemes. The projection $V_T\to U_T$ is the scheme base change of $p$, hence surjective etale by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The composite $V_T\to T$ is etale by the hypothesis on $qp$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] with its $(T,X,Y)=(T,U_T,V_T)$ to obtain that $U_T\to T$ is etale. Since $T$ was arbitrary, $q$ is representable etale by [def-trf-algebraic-space].

For the identity of an algebraic space, composition with a representable etale scheme chart is that same chart; hence the identity is chartwise etale. If $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ are chartwise etale and $U\to X$ is a representable etale scheme chart, first $U\to Y$ is representable etale by the definition of $f$, and then $U\to Z$ is representable etale by the definition of $g$. This proves composition. An isomorphism is representable etale by step 2, so its composite with a scheme chart is representable etale by the same step. It is therefore chartwise etale too. The maps and the charts here have exactly the meanings in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tags 03FR and 03FT (lemma-composition-etale); identity and isomorphism cases of the definition

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be chartwise etale, let $X'\to Y$ be arbitrary, and put $P=X\times_Y X'$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $U\to X$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Since $f$ is chartwise etale, $U\to Y$ is representable etale. Consequently $R=U\times_Y X'\to X'$ is representable etale by step 2. Given any representable etale scheme chart $W\to P$, form $Q=W\times_P R=W\times_X U$. The second expression makes $Q$ a scheme and $Q\to W$ a surjective etale scheme map, by the atlas's scheme tests. The first makes $Q\to R$ representable etale, as the base change of $W\to P$. Step 2 then makes $Q\to X'$ representable etale. Apply step 4 to $Q\to W\to X'$ to conclude that $W\to X'$ is representable etale. Since $W$ was arbitrary, $P\to X'$ is chartwise etale. The equality between the two expressions for $Q$ is the explicit reassociation of the compatible tuples $(w,u)$ with their common image in $X$.

source.place: Tag 03FU (lemma-base-change-etale): atlas proof with its omitted verification supplied by scheme tests and source descent

proof.text: For later cancellation, suppose $A,B$ are schemes, $F$ is an algebraic space, $a:A\to F$ and $b:B\to F$ are representable etale, and $r:A\to B$ satisfies $br=a$. By step 1 the fibre product $E=A\times_F B$ is a scheme, and both projections $\pi_A,\pi_B$ are etale by the scheme-test definition [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The graph $s=(\operatorname{id}_A,r):A\to E$ satisfies $\pi_A s=\operatorname{id}_A$. The identity is etale by step 2, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](3), applied to the scheme maps $s,\pi_A$, makes $s$ etale. Clause (2) then makes $r=\pi_Bs$ etale. This is a two-application consequence of scheme cancellation and composition, not a separate algebraic-space permanence assumption.

source.place: Tag 03EC(2); elementary graph-section argument using morphisms.tex Tags 02GW and 02GN

proof.text: Suppose $g:X\to Z$, $h:Y\to Z$ are chartwise etale and $hf=g$. Given a representable etale scheme chart $a:U\to X$, choose a representable surjective etale atlas $b:V\to Y$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The fibre product $W=U\times_Y V$ is a scheme by step 1, and $p:W\to U$ is surjective etale by the scheme tests for $b$. Let $r:W\to V$ be the other projection. Both $ga:U\to Z$ and $hb:V\to Z$ are representable etale by the two chartwise hypotheses. Therefore $gap:W\to Z$ is representable etale by step 2. Since $(hb)r=gap$, step 7 makes $r$ an etale scheme map. Step 2 makes $br=fap$ representable etale; step 4 then makes $fa:U\to Y$ representable etale. This proves that $f$ is chartwise etale, for every $U$ as required.

source.place: Tag 03FV (lemma-etale-permanence); choose the source presentation by U times_Y V and use Tag 03EC(2),(3)

proof.text: Use the definition of covering in the statement. An isomorphism is chartwise etale by step 5, and its inverse lifts every field-valued section over the same field, so it is a singleton covering. For composable covering families $X_i\to X$ and $X_{ij}\to X_i$, the composites are chartwise etale by step 5. Given a section $x$ of $X$ over a field $K$, [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] gives $i$, an extension $K\hookrightarrow L$, and $y\in X_i(L)$ mapping to $x|_L$. Applying the same definition to $y$ gives $j$, an extension $L\hookrightarrow M$, and $z\in X_{ij}(M)$ mapping to $y|_M$. The composite field embedding $K\hookrightarrow M$ and $z$ lift $x|_M$, because restrictions and the given natural transformations compose. Thus the composite family is jointly surjective and is a covering. This also handles empty index sets: whenever a target field-valued section exists, the covering hypothesis supplies the required index.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), clauses (1),(2); omitted point-lifting argument expanded using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU

proof.text: Finally let $\{X_i\to X\}$ be a covering and $a:X'\to X$ any map. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] each sheaf $P_i=X'\times_X X_i$ is an algebraic space; step 6 makes $P_i\to X'$ chartwise etale. For $x'\in X'(\operatorname{Spec}K)$, apply [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] to $a(x')$. Obtain $i$, a field extension $K\hookrightarrow L$, and $y\in X_i(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ with $f_i(y)=a(x')|_L$. The pair $(x'|_L,y)$ is exactly a section of the sheaf fibre product $P_i$ and lifts $x'|_L$. Thus the new family is jointly surjective and is a covering. No representability of $X_i\to X$ is used: from the existing fibre-product node we use only closure under fibre products, not its covering clause, which assumes representable etaleness. If the given index set is empty, any field-valued section of $X'$ would give one of $X$, contradicting the covering hypothesis; hence the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), clause (3); field-extension lifting supplies its omitted proof

lean.statement: theorem chartwise_etale_permanence {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ (T : Over S) (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : schemeSpace T ⟶ Y), IsChartwiseEtale f ↔ IsEtale f.hom.hom) ∧ (∀ X : AlgebraicSpace S, IsChartwiseEtale (𝟙 X)) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), IsChartwiseEtale f → IsChartwiseEtale g → IsChartwiseEtale (f ≫ g)) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z), IsChartwiseEtale f → IsChartwiseEtale (enlargedFibreProductFst g f)) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : X ⟶ Z) (h : Y ⟶ Z) (f : X ⟶ Y), IsChartwiseEtale g → IsChartwiseEtale h → f ≫ h = g → IsChartwiseEtale f) ∧ (∀ (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (e : X ≅ Y), IsChartwiseEtale e.hom ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ e.hom.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) (J : I → Type v) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (Xᵢ : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (Xᵢⱼ : ∀ i : I, J i → AlgebraicSpace S) (f : ∀ i : I, Xᵢ i ⟶ X) (g : ∀ (i : I) (j : J i), Xᵢⱼ i j ⟶ Xᵢ i), ((∀ i : I, IsChartwiseEtale (f i)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (f i).hom.hom)) → (∀ i : I, (∀ j : J i, IsChartwiseEtale (g i j)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun j : J i ↦ (g i j).hom.hom)) → (∀ a : Sigma J, IsChartwiseEtale (g a.1 a.2 ≫ f a.1)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun a : Sigma J ↦ (g a.1 a.2 ≫ f a.1).hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) (X X' : AlgebraicSpace S) (Xᵢ : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (f : ∀ i : I, Xᵢ i ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X), ((∀ i : I, IsChartwiseEtale (f i)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (f i).hom.hom)) → (∀ i : I, IsChartwiseEtale (enlargedFibreProductFst g (f i))) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (enlargedFibreProductFst g (f i)).hom.hom))
